title: Out-of-tree kube-scheduler plugins must be rebuilt for the 1.33 framework (UpdatePodToleration rename)

detection.reason: whether a custom scheduler binary is in use is not visible in the inventory

quote: Renamed `UpdatePodTolerations` action type to `UpdatePodToleration`. Action required for custom plugin developers to update their code to follow the rename.
remediation: Only clusters running a custom-built kube-scheduler with out-of-tree plugins are affected; rebuild against the 1.33 framework before rolling the control plane.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'  # an image other than registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler is a custom build

title: Service annotation service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode is deprecated — use spec.trafficDistribution
quote: The beta annotation `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` is now considered deprecated and will not graduate to GA. It remains operational for backward compatibility.
remediation: Replace the annotation with `spec.trafficDistribution: PreferClose` on each Service; the annotation keeps working for now but has no removal-free future.
verifyCommand: kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode"] != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each one should move to spec.trafficDistribution

title: Pod status.resize is no longer set — resize progress is reported through PodResizeInProgress / PodResizePending conditions

detection.reason: which client reads the field is a runtime behaviour, not a collected object

quote: The pod `status.resize` field is now deprecated and will no longer be set. The status of a pod resize will be exposed under two new conditions: `PodResizeInProgress` and `PodResizePending` instead.
remediation: Controllers or scripts that wait on `status.resize` (e.g. for `Proposed`/`InProgress`) never see it populated after the upgrade; read the two conditions instead.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.resize != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + .status.resize'  # pods still carrying the legacy field mid-resize
coversNotes: For the `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature, the API server will no longer set the resize

title: core/v1 Endpoints is deprecated — consumers should read EndpointSlice

detection.reason: every Service has an Endpoints object, so its presence is not a signal; the consumers are what matters and they are not collected

quote: The v1 Endpoints API is now officially deprecated (though still fully supported). The API will not be removed, but all users should use the EndpointSlice API instead.
remediation: No object has to change (the endpoints controller keeps writing them), but controllers, service meshes and monitoring that watch Endpoints should move to `discovery.k8s.io/v1` EndpointSlice; Endpoints also truncate above 1000 addresses.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.rules[]? | (.resources // []) | index("endpoints")) | .metadata.name' | grep -v '^system:'  # non-system principals still granted the deprecated resource

title: DRA adminAccess claims are only allowed in namespaces labelled resource.k8s.io/admin-access

detection.reason: DRA objects are not collected; pods that reference claims are, so the hint names them

quote: only users with access to an admin namespace with the `kubernetes.io/dra-admin-access` label are authorized to create ResourceClaim or ResourceClaimTemplate objects with the `adminAccess` field in this admin namespace
remediation: Label the namespaces that legitimately hold `adminAccess: true` claims with `resource.k8s.io/admin-access: "true"` before upgrading, or the claims (and the pods referencing them) are rejected. (The changelog names the label `kubernetes.io/dra-admin-access`; the 1.33 source constant `DRAAdminNamespaceLabelKey` is `resource.k8s.io/admin-access`, and 1.34 renames it to `resource.kubernetes.io/admin-access`.)
verifyCommand: kubectl get resourceclaims,resourceclaimtemplates -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(..; .adminAccess? == true)) | .metadata.namespace' | sort -u | while read ns; do echo "$ns label=$(kubectl get ns $ns -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.resource\.k8s\.io/admin-access}')"; done  # every namespace listed must show label=true

title: DRA allocationMode: All no longer schedules onto nodes with zero matching devices

detection.reason: DRA objects are not collected; pods that reference claims are, so the hint names them

quote: Kubernetes 1.33 changes that to only picking nodes which have at least one device.
remediation: Pods whose claim requests `allocationMode: All` and that today land on device-less nodes stay Pending after the upgrade; use a prioritized list with a `count: 0` alternative if that placement was intended.
verifyCommand: kubectl get resourceclaimtemplates,resourceclaims -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(..; .allocationMode? == "All")) | .kind + "/" + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # these can no longer be satisfied by a node without devices

title: Pod nodeAffinity requirement values are now validated at create time

detection.reason: the check is per requirement (operator × value shape); the projection keeps operators and values but the evaluator cannot correlate them

quote: Implemented validation for `NodeSelectorRequirement` values in Kubernetes when creating pods.
remediation: New pods whose `nodeAffinity` uses `Gt`/`Lt` with a non-integer value, or `In`/`NotIn` with a value that is not a valid label value, are rejected after the upgrade; existing pods keep running but their workload cannot roll. Fix the template before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,sts,ds,job,cronjob -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .kind + "/" + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name as $n | [.. | .nodeSelectorTerms? // empty | .[] | .matchExpressions[]? | select(.operator == "Gt" or .operator == "Lt") | select(.values[]? | test("^[0-9]+$") | not)] | select(length != 0) | $n'  # Gt/Lt requirements with a non-integer value are rejected at 1.33

title: In-place resize: memory limits cannot shrink without RestartContainer, and resizePolicy is immutable

detection.reason: the constraint binds on a future resize request, not on a stored field

quote: Memory limits cannot be decreased unless the memory resize restart policy is set to `RestartContainer`. Container resizePolicy is no longer mutable.
remediation: Automation that lowers memory limits in place must set `resizePolicy[memory].restartPolicy: RestartContainer` on the container first; a later change of `resizePolicy` itself is rejected, so set it when the pod is created.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resizePolicy != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # pods that opted into in-place resize and are bound by the new rule

title: ServiceCIDR is GA — any principal that can create ServiceCIDR objects can extend the cluster Service range

detection.reason: the concern is policy (who may create ServiceCIDRs), which is not a collected object; existing ServiceCIDRs are not collected either

quote: **Action required** for Kubernetes cluster administrators and for distributions that manage the cluster Service CIDR. Kubernetes now allows users to define the cluster Service CIDR via an API object: ServiceCIDR.
remediation: Decide who may create `networking.k8s.io/v1` ServiceCIDR objects and whether additional ranges may overlap other networks; add a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (the note gives an example) or RBAC restriction before the upgrade if only the default range should exist.
verifyCommand: kubectl get servicecidrs -o wide; kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicies -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.matchConstraints.resourceRules[]?.resources[]? == "servicecidrs") | .metadata.name'  # no policy listed means any ServiceCIDR creator can add ranges

title: ClusterTrustBundle moves to v1beta1 — kubelet projection needs the v1beta1 API served

detection.reason: the --runtime-config flag lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: In order for the `ClusterTrustBundleProjection` feature to work on the kubelet side, the `ClusterTrustBundle` API must be available at `v1beta1` version and the `ClusterTrustBundleProjection` feature gate must be enabled.
remediation: If `--runtime-config` enables `certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1` for ClusterTrustBundle, enable `certificates.k8s.io/v1beta1` as well before rolling the control plane, then restart kubelets; otherwise pods with a `clusterTrustBundle` projected volume stop mounting.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -- --runtime-config  # certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1=true without v1beta1=true breaks the projection at 1.33

title: resource.k8s.io/v1beta1 is deprecated — DRA drivers and clients should move to v1beta2 (or v1 from 1.34)

detection.reason: DRA objects are not collected and the version a driver speaks is not visible; pods that reference claims mark the clusters that care

quote: The `resource.k8s.io/v1beta1` API is deprecated and will be removed in 1.36. Use `v1beta2` instead.
remediation: Upgrade DRA drivers and any client that reads ResourceClaims/ResourceSlices at v1beta1 to a release that speaks v1beta2 (or `resource.k8s.io/v1`, GA in 1.34). The removal the note announces for 1.36 did not happen — v1beta1 is still served in 1.36 and 1.37 — so this is a deprecation, not a deadline.
verifyCommand: kubectl get --raw /metrics | grep 'apiserver_requested_deprecated_apis.*group="resource.k8s.io".*version="v1beta1"'  # any hit is a client still on v1beta1

title: Aggregated discovery v2beta1 is off by default — clients that only speak v2beta1 fall back to unaggregated discovery

detection.reason: which discovery version clients negotiate is not a collected object

quote: `apidiscovery.k8s.io/v2beta1` API group is disabled by default
remediation: kubectl and client-go from 1.30+ negotiate `apidiscovery.k8s.io/v2`; older clients still work but issue one request per group. Re-enable with `--runtime-config=apidiscovery.k8s.io/v2beta1=true` only if a client demonstrably needs it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get --raw /metrics | grep 'apiserver_request_total.*apidiscovery.k8s.io.*v2beta1' | head  # non-zero counts are clients that will fall back after the upgrade

title: Pods with supplementalGroupsPolicy: Strict are rejected by kubelets on nodes whose runtime does not support it

detection.reason: supplementalGroupsPolicy is not in the pod projection and node feature flags are not collected

quote: kubelet now rejects pods with `.spec.securityContext.supplementalGroupsPolicy: Strict` when scheduled to the node that does not support the feature (`.status.features.supplementalGroupsPolicy: false`).
remediation: Before enabling the (now on-by-default) beta, confirm every node reports `status.features.supplementalGroupsPolicy: true` (containerd 2.0+ / CRI-O 1.31+); a Strict pod landing on an older node fails admission on that kubelet instead of running with the merged groups.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns='NODE:.metadata.name,SGP:.status.features.supplementalGroupsPolicy,RUNTIME:.status.nodeInfo.containerRuntimeVersion'; kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.securityContext.supplementalGroupsPolicy == "Strict") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a Strict pod can only run on a node whose SGP column is true
coversNotes: KEP-3619: fined-grained supplemental groups policy is graduated to Beta. Note that kubelet
